blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof wala sawal hai: L.H.S. (left side) se shuru kar ke R.H.S. (right side) tak pohanchna hai.
Left side par do angles ke jama ka sine hai, to usay khol dena (expand karna) pehla kaam hai.
Plan: \(\sin(A + B)\) ka formula, phir \(\sin 45^{\circ} = \cos 45^{\circ} = 1/\sqrt{2}\), aur aakhir mein common factor bahar.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: ek identity.
Saabit karna hai: L.H.S. \(= \sin(45^{\circ} + \alpha)\) barabar hai R.H.S. \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha)\) ke.
Tareeqa: L.H.S. ko is formula se expand karenge:
\[\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B\]
Proof mein hamesha zyada mushkil (complicated) side se shuru karte hain; yahan left side ka bracket khul sakta hai, is liye wahi se.

Left side expand karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \sin(45^{\circ} + \alpha)\]
\[= \sin 45^{\circ}\cos\alpha + \cos 45^{\circ}\sin\alpha\]
Kyun: Formula mein \(A = 45^{\circ}\) aur \(B = \alpha\) rakha. Pattern \"sin cos + cos sin\" hai.

Special values rakhein
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha\]
Kyun: 45 degree par sine aur cosine dono \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) hote hain, kyunke 45-45-90 triangle ki dono chhoti sides barabar hoti hain.

Common factor bahar nikalein
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha) = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Dono terms mein \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) mushtarik (common) hai, usay bahar le aaye. Jama mein tarteeb badalne se farq nahi parta, is liye \(\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha = \sin\alpha + \cos\alpha\).

Tasdeeq, \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\) rakh kar
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \sin 90^{\circ} = 1\]
\[\text{R.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Identity har angle ke liye sahi honi chahiye; ek angle rakh kar dekhna tez tasdeeq hai. Dono sides 1 aayin.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi proof hai, is dafa cosine of a sum.
Left side ko expand kar ke 45 degree ki values rakhni hain.
Plan: \(\cos(A + B)\) ka formula, phir \(1/\sqrt{2}\) common.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: ek identity.
Saabit karna hai: \(\cos(\alpha + 45^{\circ}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)\).
Tareeqa: L.H.S. ko is formula se kholenge:
\[\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B\]
Is formula ki khaas baat yeh hai ke angle mein plus ho to beech mein minus aata hai.

Left side expand karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos(\alpha + 45^{\circ})\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos 45^{\circ} - \sin\alpha\sin 45^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(A = \alpha\), \(B = 45^{\circ}\). Pattern \"cos cos, sin sin\" aur sign ulta.
Dhyan dein: Yahan plus likh diya to R.H.S. ka minus kabhi nahi milega. Isi minus ki wajah se R.H.S. mein \(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha\) hai.

Common factor bahar nikalein
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha) = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Dono terms mein \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) common hai. Yahan tarteeb ahem hai: minus mein terms ki jagah badalne se sign badal jata hai, is liye \(\cos\alpha\) pehle hi rehna chahiye.

Tasdeeq, \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\) rakh kar
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos 90^{\circ} = 0\]
\[\text{R.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(0) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\cos 45^{\circ} - \sin 45^{\circ} = 0\), to right side bhi zero; dono barabar.
